variable.name: Surface Soil Moisture
variable.desc: Water content of the top soil layer as a fraction of saturation — early warning sign of flash drought
variable.plain: Water in just the top layer of soil, from 0 to 1.
variable.trend_means: Responds within days to rainfall, so it is the earliest warning sign of flash drought.

provenance.access: Automatic CMR discovery → authenticated OPeNDAP native-grid subset → local cache
provenance.aggregation: Native-cell polygon overlap × cos(latitude); at least 80% selected area each month
provenance.quality: Provider fill values/masks excluded; model reanalysis, not a direct measurement at every location

variable.name: Land Evaporation
variable.desc: Mean evaporation flux over land, expressed as water depth per day
variable.plain: Water evaporating from bare ground and open water, without the plant part.
variable.trend_means: Tracks how quickly the land surface itself dries out.

provenance.access: Automatic CMR discovery → authenticated OPeNDAP native-grid subset → local cache
provenance.aggregation: Native-cell polygon overlap × cos(latitude); at least 80% selected area each month
provenance.quality: Provider fill values/masks excluded; model reanalysis, not a direct measurement at every location

variable.name: Precipitation
variable.desc: Bias-corrected total precipitation (rain and snow), averaged over the month
variable.plain: How much rain and snow falls, averaged over each day of the month. 1 mm/day is about 30 mm of rain in a month.
variable.trend_means: Rising means more water arriving. Falling means drier months — the first signal of drought.

couplings.title: Surface Soil Moisture <-> Land Evaporation Coupling
couplings.description: Co-trend association. Possible mechanism: Observed correlation of r = 0.93 between Surface Soil Moisture and Land Evaporation across the analyzed timeline.

couplings.title: Surface Hydrological Recharge
couplings.description: Co-trend association. Possible mechanism: Topsoil wetness directly responds to precipitation events. Divergence indicates rapid runoff or high evaporative loss preventing rainfall infiltration into the soil layer.

couplings.title: Land Evaporation <-> Precipitation Coupling
couplings.description: Co-trend association. Possible mechanism: Observed correlation of r = 0.73 between Land Evaporation and Precipitation across the analyzed timeline.
